cards.explanation: The answer is the Day of the LORD's anger. Zephaniah stacks up his hurry-ups, and the last one says “…before the Day of the LORD’s anger comes upon you.” (Zephaniah 2:2) He also says the day passes “like chaff,” which is light stuff that blows away. So he isn't pointing at a party, friends. He's pointing at a day that's coming.

The answer is to seek the LORD. Zephaniah says, “Seek the LORD, all you humble of the earth who carry out His justice.” (Zephaniah 2:3) Then he adds two more, “Seek righteousness; seek humility.” Nobody is told to go find a hiding spot first. I think the whole point is to go toward Him.

The answer is False, and it all hangs on a little word. The verse says “Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD’s anger.” (Zephaniah 2:3) A promise would say surely, and Zephaniah doesn't. So the humble are told to seek the LORD, and the rest is left open.

The answer is abandoned. The verse says, “…Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon left in ruins.” (Zephaniah 2:4) Abandoned means the people are gone. Picture a kitchen with every cookie sheet hauled off and nobody left to flip the oven on. That's the first city on his list.

The answer is the Philistines. Zephaniah spells it out: “…O Canaan, land of the Philistines…” (Zephaniah 2:5) So the word of the LORD is against the Philistines' land on that seacoast. He names the Cherethites in the same breath. The verse doesn't leave you guessing.

The answer is True, friends. The verse says, “So the seacoast will become a land of pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.” (Zephaniah 2:6) The cities named a verse earlier give way to shepherd country. Wells for the shepherds, folds for the sheep.

The answer is the remnant of Judah. The verse says, “The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah…” (Zephaniah 2:7) A remnant is the ones who are left. So the coast ends up with the leftover folks from Judah's house. And they find pasture there.

The answer is True. They “…will lie down in the evening among the houses of Ashkelon…” (Zephaniah 2:7) That's the same Ashkelon that was “…left in ruins.” back in verse 4. Now there are folks lying down there in the evening, and that's quite a switch.

The answer is restore. The verse says, “…for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their captives.” (Zephaniah 2:7) Restore is a word I'm fond of. I sat dusty and forgotten in a junk drawer myself before I was called out of it. So when I hear about captives being restored, I perk right up.

The answer is borders. The LORD says Moab and the Ammonites “…have taunted My people and threatened their borders.” (Zephaniah 2:8) So the words came with a threat to the edges of the land. Think of a neighbor who keeps eyeing your side of the fence. That's not a friendly wave.

The answer is Sodom and Gomorrah. The LORD says, “surely Moab will be like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah…” (Zephaniah 2:9) Sodom and Gomorrah were the cities where the LORD rained down sulfur and fire (Genesis 19:24). So the picture is a place left empty. The verse goes on to call it “…a place of weeds and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland.”

The answer is True, bakers. The LORD says, “The remnant of My people will plunder them; the remainder of My nation will dispossess them.” (Zephaniah 2:9) The job goes to the remnant of His people. He says it twice, once as remnant and once as remainder.

The answer is pride. The text says, “This they shall have in return for their pride, for taunting and mocking the people of the LORD of Hosts.” (Zephaniah 2:10) Back in verse 8 the LORD said they “…have taunted My people…” (Zephaniah 2:8) So that taunting shows up again here, tied to pride.

The answer is that they will bow in worship to Him. That's the finish of the verse: “Then the nations of every shore will bow in worship to Him, each in its own place.” (Zephaniah 2:11) Each nation does it in its own place. So it's not one big crowd in one spot. It's every shore.

The answer is Assyria. The verse says, “And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria…” (Zephaniah 2:13) Right after that comes Nineveh. The verse names the nation first and then the city.

The answer is True, friends. The verse says, “He will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as a desert.” (Zephaniah 2:13) Zephaniah puts it right after He will “…destroy Assyria…” in the same verse. Dry as a desert is quite the picture.

The answer is herds and owls. The verse says, “Herds will lie down in her midst, creatures of every kind.” (Zephaniah 2:14) Both the desert owl and screech owl will roost atop her pillars. Not a crowd that pays rent.

The answer is that no one else compares to her. Nineveh thinks to herself, “I am it, and there is none besides me…” (Zephaniah 2:15) That's a city saying there's none besides her. Zephaniah calls her a “…carefree city that dwells securely…”

The answer is False, bakers. The verse gives hissing, not weeping. “Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.” (Zephaniah 2:15) That's the reaction the text gives for passersby of ruined Nineveh.
